articles.description: 在西方文学的长河里，同一位古希腊英雄曾有过两次截然不同的命运转折。 在荷马史诗《奥德赛》中，奥德修斯历尽十年漂泊，拒绝了女神赐予的长生不老与永恒青春。他动用所有的智慧与隐忍，只为穿过惊涛骇浪，回到故乡伊萨卡，与妻儿团聚。 然而，到了中世纪诗人但丁的《神曲》中，这位拉丁名为“尤利西斯”的英雄却被彻底改写——他放弃了故乡与家庭的责任，在垂暮之年依然渴望探索未知的尽头，鼓动年迈的船员驶出直布罗陀海峡，最终在永不满足的探索欲中船毁人亡。 从“奥德修斯的归家”到“尤利西斯的远航”，恰恰隐喻了人类从古典走向现代的精神转向。 01 从文艺复兴的“魔法”到现代人的“无家可归” 学者吴功青在《魔化与除魔》及解读但丁《神曲》的文章中，敏锐地捕捉到了这一现代性困境的源头。 文艺复兴哲学家皮科·米兰多拉曾宣告，人没有固定的本性，人是“自己的塑造者”，甚至可以通过“自然魔法”认识并驾驭宇宙。现代世界正是建立在这样一种双重逻辑之上： 一方面是对自然的“除魔”，剥离万物的神圣与神秘，将其还原为冰冷的物理法则；另一方面则是对人的“魔化”，人将操控自然的权柄收归己有，站在了世界的中央。 然而，当人把自然的魔力全部祛除，自己又像掌握了终极魔法一样无限扩张欲望时，危机也随之而来。人虽然赢得了掌控世界的自由，却也切断了与传统的联结，失去了敬畏与精神家园，沦为了但丁笔下那个漂泊无依的尤利西斯——一个精神上“无家可归的现代人”。 今天，这种现代性困境正在人工智能的浪潮中迎来最新的演进。 当大语言模型与生成式AI普及，普通人只需通过自然语言下达指令，就能像昔日的程序员、设计师或学者一样生成代码、剪辑大片、撰写长文。AI赋予了每个人一根近似于“皮科魔法”的魔杖。 但这种突如其来的“无所不能”，却让我们陷入了比以往任何时候都更强烈的悬浮感与无家可归的焦虑。 02 为什么拥有了强大的造物能力，我们反而感到更加漂泊？ 首先，是工具理性狂奔下的“目标迷失”。 AI极大降低了创造的门槛，让人很容易陷入一种惯性：因为“能做”，所以不停地做；因为“高效”，所以不断开辟新的战场。我们像但丁笔下的尤利西斯一样，在无限的信息海域中盲目远航，手段极其强大，终极目的却一片空白。 在无数个被AI加速启动的项目背后，我们很少停下来问一句：我到底要回到哪里？我的“伊萨卡”究竟在何处？ 其次，是“体感”与“在场感”的剥离。 正如学者程乐松在《留白》中所警惕的“心智外包”，当代码是AI写的、文案是AI生成的、创意是AI拼凑的，人与作品之间便失去了传统工匠那种一锤一凿的“摩擦感”与肉身联结。 我们虽然拥有了惊人的产出，内心却无比清楚，这些光鲜的结果并非完全源自自身生命的积淀。这种跳过思考与打磨直接获取答案的捷径，带来的是虚假的掌控感与深层的空心化焦虑。 更现实的是，边界的消失催生了“无限内卷”。 当所有普通人都被AI武装到牙齿，“无所不能”便不再是优势，而成了新的及格线。人们失去了传统职业分工和技能壁垒所提供的稳定坐标，彻底脱离了固定的位置，不得不在无限的可能性中永远奔跑、永远对比、永远害怕被时代抛弃。 03 在AI的“魔法时代”，我们该如何为自己“安家”？ 面对AI时代的“魔法诱惑”，我们该如何为自己重新安家？答案或许就藏在古典智慧与现代哲思的交汇处——重新找回“奥德修斯的航向”，并为高速运转的生命留出恰当的“留白”。 第一，分清“能做什么”与“值得为什么而做”。 技术可以无限扩展我们能力的外延，却无法替我们决定什么是有意义的。在动用AI这根魔法棒之前，我们需要先在内心确立自己真正的“伊萨卡”——或许是一段真实的家庭关系，或许是内心真正热爱的某件具体小事，又或许是生活中亟待解决的一个真实痛点。 让技术服务于你的生活，而不是让你的生活沦为技术的试验场。 第二，在看重的事情上，保留一部分“亲手打磨”的笨拙。 不要把所有的思考与创作都交给AI一键生成。允许自己慢下来，去经历阅读和创作中那种“扞格不入”的卡顿、挣扎甚至犯错。只有通过自身真实的时间与精力投入，人与世界之间才能建立起扎实的情感锚点，那份令人不安的悬浮感才会随之消散。 第三，重新肯认人的“有限性”，警惕“效率反噬”。 很多人用AI提高了工作效率，结果却发现自己更累了——因为省下来的时间立刻被用来承接更多任务，陷入了无休止的自我压榨。 真正的“留白”，是AI帮你用两小时干完了过去四小时的活，而你把省下的那两小时还给生活：去散步、发呆、陪家人吃一顿饭，或者仅仅是安静地读一本“无用”的闲书。 写在最后 在AI时代，写多少行代码、码多少字已经不再是衡量个人价值的唯一标尺。把成就感重新锚定在机器无法替代的维度上吧——去提出一个源自真实困惑的好问题，去体察他人未曾言说的情绪需求，去为最终的选择承担起作为人的责任。 终有一天我们会明白，真正的自由，不是像尤利西斯那样在无边无际的欲望海域中永无止境地漂泊；而是像奥德修斯一样，看遍世间奇景、历尽千帆之后，依然认得回家的路，在有限而具体的日常里，安顿好自己那颗渴望家园的心。
articles.title: 从奥德修斯的归帆到AI时代的魔法：无所不能的我们，为何越来越“无家可归”？

articles.author: Hillary Lovric
articles.description: AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work. Today we're releasing updates that help your team get more done: build and run business-process flows in chat, triage your day in the updated web app, get more complete answers from multiple agents at once, and connect new data sources like Meta ads and Amplitude.
articles.title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together

articles.author: Ravi Yadav
articles.description: Self-hosting LLMs on GPUs means paying to recompute the same context on every turn. Distributed KV caching with Amazon ElastiCache can cut inference cost by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%. This post walks through the distributed KV caching skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS, which evaluates and sets up the cache from your coding agent.
articles.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill

articles.author: Austin Cherian
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers managed cluster extensions for observability and user management, bringing declarative, API- and console-driven configuration to the software running on Slurm cluster nodes. This post explains how the extensions work and follows a platform team through a quarter of running a shared Slurm cluster with them.
articles.title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm

articles.author: Dmitry Soldatkin
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod introduces the Global Inference Gateway, one managed endpoint that routes inference requests across your HyperPod clusters in one Region or across Regions. It picks the best cluster, fails over automatically, and authenticates every request with SigV4 and IAM over AWS PrivateLink.
articles.title: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Global Inference Gateway: One endpoint across Regions and clusters

articles.author: Tala Qraitem
articles.description: Standard Bank Group automated the evidence behind its generative AI approval gates. Working with AWS Professional Services, the bank built an assessment in its own AWS account that scores each use case against international AI standards and its own policies using LLM-as-a-judge on Amazon Bedrock, giving risk committees consistent, traceable evidence.
articles.title: How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI

articles.author: Keith Mascarenhas
articles.description: Announcing the general availability of Amazon Textract Insights, a new generative AI feature of Amazon Textract. Describe the fields you need in natural language, submit a document or a mixed packet, and receive structured results with a confidence score and page-level grounding for each value, with no model training required.
articles.title: Announcing Amazon Textract Insights: Verifiable generative AI for documents

articles.author: Aryaman Kothari
articles.description: This second installment reviews 13 more Amazon SageMaker AI inference launches from 2026, spanning configuration recommendations, fitting more models onto each GPU, serving models too large for one instance, cross-Region routing, and post-launch tuning, bringing the year's total to 26.
articles.title: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 launches in review, part 2

articles.author: Alex Thewsey
articles.description: Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 adds a native Amazon Bedrock provider, so you can connect the open source coding agent to models like Kimi K3.1 Pro using your standard AWS credential chain (named profiles or SSO) instead of a separate API key. This post shows how to configure the provider and send your first request.
articles.title: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Madhu Samhitha Vangara
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments now supports AWS Marketplace, so agents can discover and buy x402-enabled products, APIs, data, and content and pay in USD on the developer's AWS bill, with no stablecoin wallets or API keys. This post walks through a research agent that finds a tool, pays per request through AWS Billing, and answers with sources.
articles.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments

articles.author: Dr. Jens Kohl
articles.description: When hundreds of agents serve thousands of developers, governance cannot be an afterthought. The BMW Group shares the practices and patterns its R&D teams use to build, govern, and operate AI agents at enterprise scale without sacrificing speed, quality, or compliance.
articles.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers

articles.author: Josh Anderson
articles.description: Most sellers do not need another AI product to learn. They need the tools and information they already use brought together, so they can see what is happening in their business and act on it.
articles.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick

articles.author: Hazim Qudah
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors your generative AI inference endpoints by default and tells you when a change could improve performance or lower cost. It tracks latency, GPU utilization, and serving configuration, then sends a finding through AWS Health with a one-click path to benchmark alternatives in SageMaker Studio before you apply any change.
articles.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints

articles.author: Sunitha Srivatsa
articles.description: For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions?  Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria […]
articles.title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews

articles.author: Evandro Franco
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness now runs on the open-source Strands harness, bringing a recommended model, task-oriented defaults, automatic prompt caching, proactive context management, and new built-in tools. It also adds lifecycle hooks so you can run deterministic allow or deny checks at defined points in the agent loop.
articles.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks

articles.author: Suyin Wang
articles.description: Voice cloning in Amazon Polly is now generally available. Give Amazon Polly a few minutes of recordings from a consenting speaker, and it builds a custom voice that reads new text in that speaker's voice. Cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly generative engine and support seven languages.
articles.title: Amazon Polly launches voice cloning: A unique voice for your brand

articles.author: Ilan Geller
articles.description: As enterprises scale AI on Amazon Bedrock, token spend can grow even as per-token prices fall. This post walks through six composable optimization levers, shows how Accenture applied them across four client engagements, and recommends a sequence for cutting AI token spend on your own workloads.
articles.title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach

articles.author: Rakesh Vangari
articles.description: Cisco and AWS used Cisco Transformation Fest and AWS AI League to turn hands-on AI learning into a culture of building. A Cisco engineer won the 2025 AWS AI League global title and 1,200 engineers competed in 2026. This post shares Cisco's journey, lessons from the 2026 winning agent built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and how to host your own league.
articles.title: From learning to leaderboard: How Cisco upskilled 1,200 engineers in agentic AI with AWS AI League

articles.author: Dmitry Soldatkin
articles.description: Cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. The router prefers its own Region and shifts new requests to another destination only when the local one can't serve reliably.
articles.title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI

articles.author: Joe McCarron
articles.description: Learn how Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway keep sensitive data out of the tools your AI agents call. Added as a gateway interceptor, Skyflow de-identifies data before any tool, model, or log sees it, and restores it for authorized callers, with no change to your agent code.
articles.title: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway

articles.author: Helen Greul
articles.description: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1, a reasoning model built for real-time complex dialog, is available today on AWS Marketplace and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. Discover it, evaluate it on your own data, and deploy it to a secure SageMaker endpoint in your own AWS account.
articles.title: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 is now on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

articles.author: Mijanur Palash
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers enhanced observability to help you diagnose GPU training issues faster. It brings together diagnostic and profiling capabilities for training workloads on both Amazon EKS and Slurm orchestrators, pinpointing issues across GPU, network, and host layers.
articles.title: Introducing enhanced infrastructure observability in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

articles.author: Muru Bhaskaran
articles.description: Learn how to run two memory-bounded Kubernetes Pods on a single NVIDIA A10G GPU using open-source NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS. This walkthrough builds a custom Amazon Linux 2023 image, installs KAI Scheduler and the GPU Fractioning Operator, and validates per-Pod GPU-memory contracts with enforcement and metrics.
articles.title: Using NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS

articles.author: Sandeep Raveesh-Babu
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization now supports Full Fine-Tuning (FFT). This post explores when FFT outperforms LoRA across key benchmarks, examines the spectral properties of model weight matrices behind the quality gap, shares practical hyperparameter tuning guidelines, and shows how to get started.
articles.title: Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) on SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization

articles.author: Summer Devlin
articles.description: Exa's neural search engine is backed by an in-house vector database, so the unit economics of embedding tens of billions of web documents drive the business. This post shares how Exa optimized embedding inference on AWS Neuron hardware (Inferentia2 and Trainium2) with custom NKI kernels, reaching a 47% gain in performance and cost per million documents.
articles.title: Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips

articles.author: Roy Allela
articles.description: Large training jobs can stall or compute wrong results even when every node looks healthy. Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now adds workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks that catch these failures sooner and raise the goodput of your training workloads.
articles.title: Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

articles.author: Dan Ferguson
articles.description: The Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard compares 70+ foundation models side by side on quality, speed, and cost, directly in SageMaker Studio. Learn what the leaderboard shows, how AWS benchmarks models, and how to go from a shortlist to a deployed model.
articles.title: Introducing the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard

articles.author: Alan Yao
articles.description: Airbnb runs evals on real engineering tasks and uses Amazon Bedrock observability to choose models for its coding agents and control production costs. This post shows how cost per task guides model selection, why production spending can differ from eval results, and how to monitor latency, manage quotas, and attribute spend.
articles.title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: InduTeja Aligeti
articles.description: Learn how to make RAG chatbot answers traceable with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, pgvector, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, logging sources, scores, and guardrail traces in SQL.
articles.title: Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL

articles.author: Aastha Paul
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports private certificate authorities (CAs), so your agents can connect to self-hosted identity providers that use a private CA. This post shows how to issue an IdP certificate with AWS Private CA, configure a credential provider to trust it, rotate the CA, and protect the certificate.
articles.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity

articles.author: Apoorva Chandra
articles.description: Learn how Salesforce uses the cross-Region inference router in Amazon SageMaker AI to turn fragmented Regional capacity into reliable model serving. Salesforce adds capacity securely across Regions and accounts while keeping its data residency commitments, and sees per request where each call was served and why.
articles.title: How Salesforce is advancing global-scale model serving with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI

articles.author: Mariah Miller
articles.description: Social Department, an AI operating system for entertainment marketing, worked with TrackIt and AWS to build QuickSearch: single-action queries that surface shareable scenes, quotable lines, memeable frames, and trend-aligned moments across large video libraries, using TwelveLabs models on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.
articles.title: How Social Department built culture-aware video discovery

articles.author: Puneeth Komaragiri
articles.description: Many enterprises run a centralized network model: one account owns every VPC and a central firewall inspects all traffic. This post shows a tested pattern for connecting Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs and MCP servers in that model, with the VPC Lattice resource gateway in the network account so every hop crosses the firewall.
articles.title: Connect Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs in a hub-and-spoke network with centralized inspection

articles.author: Mariah Miller
articles.description: Stretto replaced its web-form lead capture with Tara, an AI voice agent built on Amazon Nova 2 Sonic that conducts bankruptcy intake interviews by phone and qualifies leads. See how Stretto, the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, and CI&T designed the voice architecture, validated it for sensitive conversations, and moved it to production.
articles.title: How Stretto built an AI voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic

articles.author: Jane Ridge
articles.description: A recap of the inaugural AWS Quick User Group DC meetup, where data leaders explored getting enterprise data ready for AI agents. It covers what's new in AWS Quick, Financial Independence Group's AI analytics journey, and hands-on app and no-code flow building.
articles.title: From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents

articles.author: Vinay Arora
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo for distributed inference, with multi-node and disaggregated serving, KV-aware routing, and automatic fault recovery. Serve large models across many nodes without building the orchestration layer yourself.
articles.title: Managed NVIDIA Dynamo on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference

articles.author: Pallav Gupta
articles.description: As production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore process multi-megabyte JSON payloads, token costs and latency climb. This post shares three composable strategies: offloading heavy artifacts to Amazon S3, on-demand result paging, and dictionary compaction. Together they cut per-turn token use by up to 71% and latency by up to 80%.
articles.title: Reducing token costs and latency in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore JSON workloads

articles.author: Meghan Kothari
articles.description: The biggest cost lever in a generative AI system is whether you call a model at all. Learn how to decide whether each workflow step needs a model, and map each option to AWS: deterministic code, a constrained decision call, or a right-sized model on Amazon Bedrock.
articles.title: Cut generative AI costs: Code for rules, models for judgment

articles.author: Dmitry Soldatkin
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache-aware routing, a new strategy that routes each request to the instance holding the longest cached match for its prompt. Learn how it works, when to use it compared with prefix-aware routing, and how to enable, invoke, and verify it on single model and inference component endpoints.
articles.title: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache aware routing

articles.author: Sana Iqbal
articles.description: Custom metadata schemas in AWS Agent Registry let an administrator define typed, validated fields that every agent, MCP server, and skill must carry. This post follows an MCP record from schema definition through registration, enrichment, approval, and discovery, so teams govern and find resources with one shared set of facts.
articles.title: Govern and discover records with common metadata in AWS Agent Registry

articles.author: Nithyashree Alwarsamy
articles.description: When an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore calls Snowflake Cortex AI over MCP, how does it authenticate? This post walks through three OAuth patterns we tested on AgentCore Identity: Snowflake OAuth, three-legged OAuth with a corporate IdP, and two-legged OAuth, so you can match your organization's identity, audit, and compliance needs.
articles.title: Secure OAuth patterns for Snowflake Cortex AI through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Varun Rajan
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker AI now offers AI data preparation capabilities for building high-quality training and evaluation data. Generate synthetic examples, assess and improve datasets, auto-label at scale, and bring in expert review through Python SDK APIs and an agent skill, all from your own notebook or IDE.
articles.title: Announcing AI data preparation capabilities in Amazon SageMaker: Build high-quality datasets for model development workflows

articles.author: Dr. Asa Kalavade
articles.description: Most enterprises have AI that works in a demo but stalls before production. AWS Forward Deployed Engineering closes that gap. AWS engineers embed with customer teams to take high-value workflows to production in 45-day sprints, leaving a foundation, workflows, and governance the customer owns.
articles.title: Getting AI out of the demo and into businesses globally

articles.author: Marco Larrea
articles.description: SMART, an open-source Python SDK and Terraform stack, deploys the full WhatsApp channel layer to your AWS account with one command. Bring any agent that runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and SMART handles webhook ingestion, media, conversation memory, scheduling, and Meta message templates.
articles.title: Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Martin Maritsch
articles.description: OpenTSLM, an open source family of time-series language models, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. See how Nexthink and Aionic Labs apply it to proactive IT support, then deploy OpenTSLM to a real-time endpoint and fine-tune it on your own data with TimeNet and a SageMaker training job.
articles.title: Reason over time-series data with OpenTSLM on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

articles.author: Michelle Ye
articles.description: AWS Quick gives your whole organization AI that knows your business, respects your security rules, and acts on your behalf. At AWS re:Invent 2026, customers including Allianz, Cox Automotive, and Southwest Airlines share how they govern, extend, and scale Quick. Use this guide to find the sessions that fit your goals.
articles.title: Your complete guide to AWS Quick at AWS re:Invent 2026

articles.author: Mariah Miller
articles.description: LoanPro worked with AWS Partner AllCloud and the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center to build a multi-agent AI assistant on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It gives loan servicing agents instant borrower context and next-best-action recommendations, reducing customer call times by up to 15 percent.
articles.title: How LoanPro built an agentic AI loan servicing assistant with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Mia Chang
articles.description: Enterprises adopting agentic AI at scale need platforms that embed responsible AI from the start. This post gives platform and application teams a three-phase roadmap (governance foundation, pilot deployment, and evaluation and hardening) that maps the AWS Responsible AI Lens pillars to each phase, with guidance on when to revisit each one.
articles.title: Responsible AI for agentic AI: A phased roadmap for platform and application teams

articles.author: Shubham Gupta
articles.description: ArisGlobal runs NavaX, its life-sciences AI engine, on Amazon Bedrock. By caching the shared prompt prefix instead of each per-case document, ArisGlobal cut effective input cost by about 50% and overall monthly inference spend by about 40%, while onboarding more tenants without proportional cost growth.
articles.title: How ArisGlobal scaled generative AI inference on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Peng Yang
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory now store conversations, extract facts, and bring long-term memory into a single AgenticRetrieveStream call. This post shows how to build a memory-aware, multi-user assistant where each user sees only the documents they may read and each user's memory stays private.
articles.title: Build memory-aware AI agents with Agentic Retrieve on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

articles.author: Rob Gates
articles.description: Duco, a data automation platform for tier-one banks, rebuilt its agentic AI stack on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. With strict per-tenant isolation, a multi-model strategy, and an MCP skills architecture that cut context overhead by 90%, Duco cut reconciliation deployment time 10x and onboarding costs 70%.
articles.title: How Duco transforms financial data automation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Malini Sethi
articles.description: Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem, not a model problem. This post gives a field-tested taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns and anti-patterns, a framework for deciding when multiple agents are warranted, and how to build cost-efficient, reliable systems on AWS.
articles.title: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing

articles.author: Ashwin Srinivasan
articles.description: MoEngage built Merlin AI, a set of AI agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that let marketing and product teams draft, analyze, and adjust campaigns from a single conversation. Learn how MoEngage turned its existing APIs into MCP tools and kept each tenant's data isolated while giving agents secure access to live platform data.
articles.title: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Abhishek Ashish
articles.description: Legacy mainframe Assembler applications are costly to maintain and hard to staff. This post presents a multi-stage, AI-powered methodology using Amazon Bedrock, Kiro IDE, and AWS Transform to extract business rules, convert Assembler through an intermediate COBOL stage, and deploy modernized Java Spring Boot applications on AWS.
articles.title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform

articles.author: Elias Bedmar
articles.description: Novo Nordisk's Manufacturing Technology team within the Tablet area team built a process-intelligence assistant on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using a GraphRAG architecture that pairs a knowledge graph in Amazon Neptune with hybrid search in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless to turn millions of controlled manufacturing documents into grounded, cited answers.
articles.title: Novo Nordisk modernizes manufacturing process documents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Josh DeMuth
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so agentic retrieval can answer questions over CSV, XLSX, and XLS files. It looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row, then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer multi-step analytical questions.
articles.title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

articles.author: Jian Zhang
articles.description: With Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, you block a content category by describing it in plain language, and the guardrail matches by meaning rather than keyword, which can block more than you intend. This post presents eight best practices for writing a topic precisely enough that the guardrail blocks what you mean and passes what you don't.
articles.title: Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

articles.author: Josh DeMuth
articles.description: Retrieval instructions in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base set the voice, format, retrieval guidance, and answer policy for each tenant on shared knowledge bases. This post shows how to give each tenant its own answers, keep tenant data apart with metadata filters, scope access with IAM tags, and roll out changes one tenant at a time.
articles.title: Customize answers per tenant in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

articles.author: Dustin Liu
articles.description: Many generative AI applications resend the same long context on every request. Prompt caching lets open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock reuse it to reduce input cost and latency. This post shows implicit and explicit caching through the Chat Completions API and applies caching to an OpenCode coding agent session.
articles.title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: WonGu Rho
articles.description: GS Caltex connects Amazon SageMaker Canvas to Amazon SageMaker Pipelines so process engineers' no-code models run in production. This post shows how ML engineers reuse validated preprocessing flows and models, cutting deployment from about a week to a few hours and running batch inference every 30 minutes.
articles.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, part 1

articles.author: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan
articles.description: Coding agents work in tasks, and the number that matters is cost per solved task, not price per token. In this post, you use the AWS CDK to deploy LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin on Amazon Bedrock, then measure cost per solved task for a routed model group against single-model baselines.
articles.title: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard

articles.author: Evandro Franco
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots your initialized environment and restores it for each new session, so session start no longer grows with image size. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and four patterns to keep work off the first request.
articles.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime

articles.author: Malav Shastri
articles.description: Deploy OpenFold3-preview from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to predict 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, and ligand complexes in your own AWS account. The post covers asynchronous inference, multi-GPU parallelism, bringing your own MSAs for accuracy and privacy, and scaling to zero to reduce cost.
articles.title: OpenFold3 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: Predict biomolecular structures

articles.author: Belair Albahagwi
articles.description: Learn how AssemblyAI runs cost-optimized speech-to-text inference at scale on AWS, using Amazon ECS, Amazon EC2 Spot GPU instances, and an Amazon SQS-based retry architecture to achieve 70% cost savings while maintaining SLA commitments across European Regions.
articles.title: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot

articles.author: Aamna Najmi
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock provides built-in, zero-instrumentation cost attribution that traces every inference call back to the IAM principal that made it. This post shows how to attribute per-user Bedrock costs for AI developer and productivity tools using IAM Identity Center, session tags, and CUR 2.0, and how to enforce per-user usage limits.
articles.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Shantanu Tripathi
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture records live inference inputs and outputs to Amazon S3. This post walks through one end-to-end example: capturing a support router's production traffic, surfacing a new-product blind spot with Amazon Athena, fine-tuning on the captured data with the HyperPod training operator, and measuring the before-and-after lift.
articles.title: Build a model improvement flywheel with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture

articles.author: Alex Nails
articles.description: SGLang-Neuron is now publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container. With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you already know, all running on native PyTorch.
articles.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron

articles.author: Ariel Jirau
articles.description: Natera built SWARM, an agentic AI system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that captures institutional lab-operations knowledge and deploys it at scale. This post walks through the full architecture, from knowledge base construction to deployment and evaluation, delivering about 130x faster first response and 96.2% automated coverage across support tickets.
articles.title: How Natera designed an agentic AI system for lab ops with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Sai Pavan Kasani
articles.description: Your Amazon Bedrock inference bill can keep climbing even after you tune prompts and application logic. Four request-level choices (cache duration, service tier, reasoning effort, and maxTokens) change how many tokens the service processes and the rate applied. We show how we tested each and how to verify the effect.
articles.title: Four Amazon Bedrock inference choices that affect cost

articles.author: Arun Chandapillai
articles.description: Get per-identity Amazon Bedrock cost visibility and enforceable spend limits using only AWS-native features, with no application code for the common case. Attribute spend with IAM principal tags, report with CUR 2.0 or Cost Explorer, and enforce with AWS Budgets actions that apply a Deny policy when a threshold is crossed.
articles.title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets

articles.author: Majd Arbash
articles.description: Comparing per-token prices hides the real cost of running a model on Amazon Bedrock. This post shows how to calculate the true cost per task across four hidden cost drivers, reduce it with caching, routing, and output constraints, and prove agent ROI with human baselines, holdout experiments, and a five-dimension scorecard.
articles.title: Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Sitaraman Vijay Krishna
articles.description: Build a self-service LLM gateway with LiteLLM on AWS Fargate that puts Amazon Bedrock foundation models behind an OpenAI-compatible API. Developers get instant access through a single API key, while platform teams gain per-user cost controls, quota isolation, and observability.
articles.title: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM

articles.author: Madhu Parthasarathy
articles.description: AI agents now run multi-step workloads for hours and act on behalf of users, raising the bar for secure, scalable agent compute. Learn how the next generation of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime delivers hardware-isolated sessions with faster starts, more compute, usage-based billing, and isolation that now extends to your data.
articles.title: Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime

articles.author: Josh DeMuth
articles.description: The migration guide in the amazon-bedrock skill helps you migrate a customer-managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base to a Managed Knowledge Base. Your coding agent plans the move with read-only discovery, creates the new knowledge base or an infrastructure-as-code template alongside the original, and validates retrieval before you cut over.
articles.title: Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent

articles.author: Amit Chaudhary
articles.description: Build a composable, interoperable multi-agent system on AWS with the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. A LangChain orchestrator on Amazon ECS communicates with a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore across organizational boundaries, using bidirectional, OAuth-authenticated calls, with neither side depending on the other's framework or SDK.
articles.title: Build composable, interoperable multi-agent systems with A2A on AWS

articles.author: Renya Kujirada
articles.description: Learn how to expose an Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base to AI agents as MCP tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway while keeping per-user access control. A request interceptor injects verified identity, Policy in AgentCore validates it independently, and a resource-based policy restricts direct access to the knowledge base.
articles.title: Fine-grained access control for Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base tools

articles.author: Yuan Wei
articles.description: Agents stall between demo and release when teams lack a repeatable way to measure how good an agent is and whether the last change helped. This post covers three agent properties that break traditional CI/CD, a measured case where an aggregate metric hides a coverage gap, and Agent DLC: one lifecycle, two loops, and one explicit standard for judging every change.
articles.title: From prototype to production: Engineering agents with Agent DLC

articles.author: Viquar Khan
articles.description: Learn how Java developers can build production-ready autonomous AI agents using Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI. This post walks through tool calling, conversation memory, resilience patterns, and multi-agent orchestration, then deploys the agent to AWS with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
articles.title: Build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI

articles.author: Shivi Bhatia
articles.description: A practical guide for enterprises rolling out OpenAI Codex to developers on AWS, with Amazon Bedrock as the model backend, covering the access, governance, and cost decisions that platform, security, and finance teams need to align on.
articles.title: OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Ferhat Erata
articles.description: A textual diff of two formal policies flags every cosmetic change and hides the one that alters behavior. This post shows how to compute a symbolic, deterministic semantic diff with an open-source anti-unification engine, so reviewers see only the genuine disagreements between two candidate authorization policies.
articles.title: Semantic diffing of formal policies with anti-unification

articles.author: Siddharth Senger
articles.description: Silent data corruption is a GPU fault that returns wrong but plausible numbers with no error, quietly poisoning distributed training. This post adds three checks to a PyTorch DDP loop to detect it, localize the faulty node on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and hand the node to automatic recovery for replacement.
articles.title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

articles.author: Shubham Divekar
articles.description: Today we're announcing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: your own code can search the web with a single signed API call, with no gateway and no resources to create. Call it from the AWS SDKs or the AWS CLI and use it in applications, agent loops, and data pipelines.
articles.title: Introducing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Tymofii Kryvtsun
articles.description: A recap of the major Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Strands updates from October 2026: new models to match each task, updates that keep agents available and grounded, and clearer cost reporting for AI builders.
articles.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in October 2026

articles.author: Markus Adhiwiyogo
articles.description: AWS re:Invent 2026 includes more than 140 AI/ML track sessions. This attendee's guide helps you find the breakouts, chalk talks, workshops, and builders' sessions that fit your role and goals, spanning AI chips, models and inference, agents, agent trust, and sustainability, so you can build a smarter re:Invent schedule.
articles.title: The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track

articles.author: Prachi Kulkarni
articles.description: This post shows how to keep the AWS Agent Registry current automatically. Using AWS CloudTrail, Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AgentCore Identity, an event-driven pipeline detects MCP server changes and pushes updated tool metadata to the registry with no stored secrets, across single- and multi-account environments.
articles.title: Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture

articles.author: Asif Fouzi
articles.description: DXC Technology runs mission-critical managed IT services for regulated organizations across 70 countries. Learn how DXC built DCX OASIS, its Human+AI operating model, on a governed multi-model substrate in Amazon Bedrock, separating a resilient model substrate from a trusted harness that orchestrates, governs, and audits AI agents at scale.
articles.title: How DXC Technology built a multi-model AI substrate on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Sabine Khan
articles.description: Every generative AI team keeps rebuilding the same components: RAG pipelines, document processors, and agent scaffolding. This post shows how to access a curated catalog of 23 production-ready, open source reusable assets from the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, with real delivery results from DoorDash, Lyft, and Ricoh.
articles.title: Accelerating generative AI delivery with reusable assets

articles.author: Vishnu Elangovan
articles.description: Learn how to build an AI-driven product development lifecycle (AI-PDLC) with a suite of six AWS Quick agents that take you from scattered customer signals to a validated prototype across Discover, Decide, Design, and Prototype, with human approval at every gate and a specification ready to hand to coding agents like Kiro.
articles.title: Accelerating product development with AI-driven lifecycle management (AI-PDLC) in AWS Quick

articles.author: Samaneh Aminikhanghahi
articles.description: The Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF) is a framework-agnostic system for evaluating AI agents. UAEF converts each framework's traces into one canonical format, scores them with 36 built-in metrics across 7 dimensions, and stores results so teams can compare agent versions and catch regressions.
articles.title: UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents

articles.author: Victor Wang
articles.description: AWS Marketplace now supports usage-based metering for Amazon SageMaker bidirectional streaming inference, so model providers can charge for what customers actually consume during a live stream. Deepgram is the launch partner, bringing usage-based speech-to-text and text-to-speech billing to AWS Marketplace.
articles.title: Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming

articles.author: Aris Tsakpinis
articles.description: Kimi K3.1 Pro from Moonshot AI is now available on Amazon Bedrock. Learn how to get started through the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, Responses, and Converse APIs, optimize inference with explicit prompt caching, and use the model as a coding assistant in OpenCode.
articles.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Sundar Raghavan
articles.description: The Web Search API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gives agents current, cited web results signed with the AWS credentials they already use. In this post, build a daily dependency watcher as a LangGraph graph that researches package ecosystems in parallel, keeps its rules in code, and checks every finding against its cited sources.
articles.title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search

articles.author: Bharathi Srinivasan
articles.description: When you deploy an agent, whether it is working is really several questions: did it finish the task, stay on topic, leak data, or skip steps? This post shows how to evaluate agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval evaluators, and how to match each behavior that matters to the right evaluator at the right level.
articles.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations

articles.author: Kushal Mangtani
articles.description: Learn how Trovata built autonomous treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using an RBAC-secured architecture for bank-branded AI deployment and agentic workflows that move corporate treasury from manual operations to real-time decision-making at enterprise scale.
articles.title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore

articles.author: Varun Valsan
articles.description: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) built an agentic test orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that turns requirements into executable, governed tests for its Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) clients. Learn how specialized agents, per-tenant isolation, and workload-aware execution cut testing effort by 88% in an internal benchmark.
articles.title: How TCS built an agentic test orchestrator with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Steph Gooch
articles.description: Running Amazon Bedrock across many accounts shows you the bill but not what happened inside each call. This post builds a centralized observability data lake that aggregates Bedrock invocation logs from every linked account into one queryable table, so you can see prompts, token counts, model choice, and per-invocation cost across your organization.
articles.title: Amazon Bedrock tokenomics data lake

articles.author: Jed Lechner
articles.description: Repeatable tasks like status updates, release notes, and ticket creation can be encoded in AWS Quick through agents and skills. This post covers how agents, skills, and your data fit together in AWS Quick, how to build and share skills for your team, and how the official catalog and custom agents help you use them.
articles.title: How skills and agents work in AWS Quick

articles.author: Siddhant Sahu
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports single-shot RAG and retrieval-only requests through AgenticRetrieveStream, alongside agentic retrieval. This post explains how the maxAgentIteration parameter matches retrieval effort to each request, using an illustrative internal banking policy assistant.
articles.title: Single-shot and agentic retrieval with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

articles.author: Dani Mitchell
articles.description: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Learn what's new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with it on Amazon Bedrock.
articles.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS

articles.author: Venu Kanamatareddy
articles.description: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B-parameter multimodal vision-language model, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. Deploy the NVFP4 or BF16 variant in a few steps, then run text, image, and video inference for document intelligence, computer-use agents, and multimodal agentic workloads.
articles.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

articles.author: Sindhura Palakodety
articles.description: A seven-layer composable reference architecture for taking enterprise agentic AI from prototype to production on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each layer has a stable contract, so you can swap technologies at any layer without redesigning the rest of the stack.
articles.title: Pluggable Agentic AI Framework: A seven-layer composable enterprise agentic AI reference architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Raphael Simon
articles.description: CrossnoKaye brought physical AI to heavy industry with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Its ATLAS platform and AURA agentic system ground AI reasoning in live plant data and run verifiable Python in isolated AgentCore sandboxes, giving plant engineers checkable, math-backed answers instead of model guesses.
articles.title: How CrossnoKaye grounds physical AI with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Kady LaBarre
articles.description: Introducing AWS Quick, formerly Amazon Quick, and the debut of our first brand campaign celebrating teams who keep business moving. AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work, where teams use AI agents to research, analyze, and act across the data and applications they already rely on.
articles.title: Professional work deserves professional tools. Meet AWS Quick.

articles.author: Shantanu Tripathi
articles.description: Amazon SageMaker Inference now supports GPU partitioning with NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which divides one GPU into hardware-isolated partitions so you can run a different model in each or take a right-sized fraction of a newer accelerator. This post shows how two optional API fields place one model per partition, and what we measured against a whole older GPU.
articles.title: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints

articles.author: Thomas Delteil
articles.description: As we built Amazon Quick, its agents grew from answering questions to taking actions, and the same primitives kept getting rebuilt under different names. This post shares the taxonomy we converged on — triggers, agents, capabilities, and learned context — found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When, What, Who, and How.
articles.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick

articles.author: Aishwarya Pawar
articles.description: Learn how to build a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate that gives AI agents secure, metadata-driven access to an enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON file, with no per-dataset integration code.
articles.title: Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate

articles.author: Hammad Ausaf
articles.description: In Part 1 you built one governed agent. Part 2 scales the pattern to an enterprise: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes the single front door and redeems Okta's grant, Cedar policies bind each tool to the agent, a second agent runs on Amazon EKS, and AgentCore Observability traces every allow and deny beside Okta's log in Amazon CloudWatch.
articles.title: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 2

articles.author: Hammad Ausaf
articles.description: An AI agent that acts for a user raises an identity question that per-app OAuth and service accounts leave open: which agent may act for which user, and how you stop it. In this first post of two, you build a task agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that governs access through Okta Cross App Access and AgentCore Identity, and enforces each user's authority.
articles.title: Govern AI agent access with Okta Cross App Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Part 1

articles.author: Adam Maksimuk
articles.description: Greenlight Financial resolves more than 90% of up to 4,000 monthly security and risk cases without human intervention using Luna, a tiered multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post covers the architecture, episodic memory for continuous learning, and the expansion from SOC operations into financial risk triage.
articles.title: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Karan Nayak
articles.description: Taxbit built Taxbit Assist, a cited, permission-aware AI assistant embedded in its enterprise dashboard, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post shows how they grounded answers in a curated knowledge base, enforced role-aware and region-compliant safety, and continuously measured answer quality on live production traffic.
articles.title: Taxbit Assist: A grounded, role-aware AI agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Andrew (Qingjie) Ren
articles.description: Run Claude Code as a remote agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Each coding task runs in its own isolated session in your AWS account, every model call goes through Amazon Bedrock, and the result comes back as a GitHub pull request you review and merge.
articles.title: Extend Claude Code to remote sessions on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with security controls

articles.author: Adrianna Chudy
articles.description: Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore returns a synthesized, source-cited answer to a natural-language question in a single tool call, with no search, retrieve, synthesize, and citation pipeline to build. Learn how it works and how to add it to an AgentCore Gateway and call it from an agent.
articles.title: Getting started with Web Answer on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: James Kim
articles.description: Learn how Amazon Marketplace evaluates A+ Content quality at scale on Amazon SageMaker AI by rendering each product page as a single snapshot, scoring it with a vision-language model fused with OCR readability signals in a CatBoost classifier, and using SHAP to turn each decision into prioritized, actionable recommendations for selling partners.
articles.title: How Amazon Marketplace evaluates content quality with Amazon SageMaker AI

articles.author: Sungyeon Kim
articles.description: Some agent-evaluation questions are narrow and repeatable, and decision models answer exactly that kind of question. This post shows how to connect two decision models, Jev and Strands Decider, to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations through code-based evaluators, and how to validate a decision-model check before you gate a release on it.
articles.title: Use decision models with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations

articles.author: Steve Vinsik
articles.description: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick reviews eligible agent actions within your existing controls, reducing unnecessary approval prompts while keeping consequential decisions with a person. See how policy sets the boundary, how a classifier reviews actions, and how AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Logs support audit.
articles.title: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters

articles.author: Yoonseo Kim
articles.description: In production AI agents, context management is the real bottleneck. This post presents a four-layer context engineering framework (architecture, prompts, file-based tools, and verification agents), implemented in working code from Deep Insight, an open source multi-agent data analysis solution on the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
articles.title: Four layers of context engineering for production AI agents: How Deep Insight applies them in working code

articles.author: Bhagyashree Chandak
articles.description: This post explores how Indegene built a production-grade, LLM-powered Data Quality Agent in its NEXT Unified Data Platform on AWS. The agent generates context-aware data quality rules, validates them, and produces ready-to-run SQL and Python under human-in-the-loop governance, helping life sciences organizations scale enterprise data quality.
articles.title: How Indegene is modernizing and scaling enterprise data quality in life sciences

articles.author: Jin Tiong Lim
articles.description: U Mobile, Malaysia's newest 5G network provider, built AiDaH, an agentic AI operations platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that moves beyond AI assistance to autonomous action across telco operations. Nine months after production launch, AiDaH handles over 150 operational scenarios across six divisions, cutting trouble tickets by up to 84.5%.
articles.title: How U Mobile built agentic telco operations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Puneeth Komaragiri
articles.description: Amazon Quick brings structured and unstructured data together in one experience. In this post, you connect Amazon S3 as a knowledge base, enrich a dataset, build a Space, and create a custom chat agent that answers business questions across both data types through a single conversational interface.
articles.title: Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick

articles.author: Greg Biegel
articles.description: Learn how to configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway for an on-behalf-of (OBO) token exchange with Microsoft Entra ID, so an AI agent can call the ServiceNow REST API while preserving the calling user's identity. AgentCore Gateway performs the exchange natively, with no interceptor Lambda or custom code.
articles.title: ServiceNow on-behalf-of token exchange with Bedrock AgentCore Gateway

articles.author: Iskander Sanchez-Rola
articles.description: Gen Digital built Norton Revamp, a generative AI-powered professional reputation management platform, with an AI-curated News Engine grounded by Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how the Gen team delivers real-time, cited content suggestions, goal setting, and news feeds with zero data egress and Norton-grade privacy.
articles.title: How Gen Digital built Norton Revamp’s AI-curated News Engine with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search

articles.author: Rajesh Nagpal
articles.description: Learn how to build a governed semantic layer for agentic AI inside EDB Postgres AI and query it from a Strands Agents agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Business meaning, join paths, and access control all live in Postgres, with GRANT and row-level security enforcing what each agent can read.
articles.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI with EDB Postgres AI and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Nolan Chen
articles.description: Learn how Cartesia, an AWS Partner, uses purpose-built State Space Models and AWS infrastructure to deliver sub-100ms text-to-speech and speech-to-text at global scale, and how to deploy its Sonic model on Amazon SageMaker AI or self-managed Amazon EC2 GPU instances.
articles.title: Building ultra-low-latency voice AI applications on AWS

articles.author: Naomi Teng
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock now offers in-country inference in India for Kimi K3, keeping processing within the Mumbai and Hyderabad Regions. This post explains the global and geographic cross-Region inference options and shares example code for reading and understanding Indic-language documents with Kimi K3.
articles.title: Introducing India-based inference for Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Daxeshkumar Patel
articles.description: This post shows how to use Crawl4AI, an open source web crawler, as a content preparation layer for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, handling JavaScript rendering, selective extraction, and custom metadata enrichment before web content reaches an Amazon S3 data source.
articles.title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI

articles.author: Giuseppe Zappia
articles.description: Agentic assistants built on frontier models run a multi-step tool loop, and paying frontier prices on every step is hard to sustain at production scale. This post shows how to use sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) to transfer a frontier teacher's agentic behavior into a small, lower-cost student on Amazon SageMaker AI.
articles.title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI

articles.author: Aishwarya Gavili
articles.description: Learn how to build a multi-agent engineering assistant that compresses aerospace component substitution evaluation from days to minutes, using Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Strands Agents SDK to assemble substitution evidence while keeping the engineer as the decision-maker.
articles.title: Agentic engineering intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Marek Klatowicz
articles.description: Circle K's DevOps team cut incident triage from 45-60 minutes to under 15 by building an agentic triage system on Amazon Bedrock. This post walks through the architecture, the initial Amazon Bedrock Flows implementation, the migration to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the lessons learned from scaling it.
articles.title: How Circle K accelerated DevOps incident triage to under 15 minutes with Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan
articles.description: This post presents a five-stage operating model for managing Amazon Bedrock cost: attribute every dollar to an owner, make every request observable, enforce budgets, optimize platform defaults, and operate a review cadence. Written for FinOps and platform engineering teams.
articles.title: Managing Amazon Bedrock costs end to end: A playbook for FinOps and platform teams

articles.author: Sundar Raghavan
articles.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Session endpoints give each runtime session an authenticated URL that forwards any HTTP method, path, and WebSocket connection to the ports you allow. In this post, you deploy a coding agent that keeps a Vite website running in its session, then watch the live site update in your browser as the agent edits files.
articles.title: Preview web apps live as your coding agent builds them with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime

articles.author: Saumya Shah
articles.description: Worldwide Express automated its less-than-truckload freight billing-exception process with a multi-agent solution built on Amazon Bedrock. Six months after launch, the company cut active exceptions by 75%, improved time-to-cash by four weeks, and unlocked $10 million in free cash flow.
articles.title: How Worldwide Express automated freight exceptions with Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Virgil Ennes
articles.description: The ChatGPT desktop app is now available on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US). This post walks through a controlled local deployment that routes model inference to Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-West) using API-mode sign-in, a managed device policy, a named AWS profile, and network restrictions, so a security team can validate it before broader use.
articles.title: Configure the ChatGPT desktop app with Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)

articles.author: Priyanka Bettaswamygowda
articles.description: The UK Amazon Quick User Group's 2026 roundup: three quarterly meetups, 150+ attendees, and customer stories from Arriva, Carsa, and Propulse Lab on using agentic AI and Amazon Quick to turn data into faster decisions, higher satisfaction, and scalable growth.
articles.title: How the UK Amazon Quick User Group grew in 2026

articles.author: Sakthi Chellapparimanam
articles.description: Epsilon's Agentic Platform team delivers UI testing as a managed, multi-tenant service built on Amazon Nova Act and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool. Tests are written in plain English and run on browsers managed by AWS, giving every product team resilient, intent-driven testing with zero per-team infrastructure overhead.
articles.title: Building intent-driven UI testing with Amazon Nova Act

articles.author: Sarat Guttikonda
articles.description: Turn a PHP-to-Java migration from a one-time leap of faith into a measurable, repeatable process with Kiro. This post walks through a reusable engine: a mechanical discovery scanner and an eight-phase, parity-first workflow that treats the original PHP application as the specification and verifies the Java port with a parity harness.
articles.title: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro

articles.author: Michelle Goodstein
articles.description: AWS Batch quota management is a new scheduling capability you can use to divide GPU capacity into quota shares per team or project, automatically lend idle capacity across shares, and use preemption to run your highest-priority SageMaker Training jobs first, all without manual coordination.
articles.title: Lend and borrow resources across teams with AWS Batch’s quota management for SageMaker Training jobs

articles.author: Nikhil Kumar
articles.description: MoEngage turned roughly 400 private REST APIs across 7 AWS Regions into permission-scoped agent tools with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. No per-service MCP servers, no public endpoints, and no 400-tool context bloat. See how OpenAPI specs, Cedar policies, and managed Amazon VPC Lattice egress made it work.
articles.title: How MoEngage turned over 400 APIs into agent tools with AgentCore Gateway

articles.author: Alex Iankoulski
articles.description: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model that pairs reasoning and tool use with multimodal understanding. This post explores its architecture and use cases, then shows how to deploy it on Amazon EKS, EKS Auto Mode, and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod EKS with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM.
articles.title: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS

articles.author: Omar Elkharbotly
articles.description: Stand up a governed, multi-account Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This post walks through the architecture and an open-source reference blueprint: the operating model, control plane, per-Workstream cells, separate inference and tool gateways, and a CI/CD evaluation pipeline that gates each agent before production.
articles.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

articles.author: Sunita Koppar
articles.description: The Ray Train Deep Learning Container ships the full CUDA-through-EFA stack, so you build no image. This post walks through a reproducible sample that fine-tunes Qwen2.5-1.5B with PyTorch FSDP across eight GPUs on two EFA-enabled g6.12xlarge instances on Amazon EKS, using the container exactly as published.
articles.title: Distributed training with Ray Train DLCs and EFA on EKS

articles.author: Vinicius Pedroni
articles.description: As QA test automation spreads across an organization, organizing tests and controlling who owns them becomes the real work. Part 3 of the QA Studio series on Amazon Nova Act adds applications that organize tests and report health metrics, plus team-based user management that controls who can see and change what.
articles.title: Accelerating software delivery with agentic QA automation using Amazon Nova Act – Part 3

articles.author: Pasquale DeMaio
articles.description: AWS has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for AWS Connect Customer. This recognition marks an important milestone for our team, and it reflects years of work pushing on what's possible in customer experience.
articles.title: AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service

articles.author: Kanwaljit Khurmi
articles.description: Seekable OCI (SOCI) indexing for Amazon SageMaker AI training and processing jobs takes full container image download off the critical path. SageMaker AI lazy-loads your image to start containers in seconds instead of minutes, with no changes to your job definition. See the benchmarks and how to adopt it.
articles.title: Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs

articles.author: Khaled Thabit
articles.description: Property Finder found that 96.8% of their vision-AI evaluation labels were inherited from the incumbent model, hiding its true accuracy. See how they built unbiased ground truth, applied evolutionary prompt optimization, and selected a more accurate, cost-effective model on Amazon Bedrock, cutting cost by 86% across 11 image-quality attributes.
articles.title: Fix evaluation bias to unlock better models on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Purna Sanyal
articles.description: In this post, we show how Exowatt used Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization to build a repeatable AI pipeline that produces task-specific fine-tuned models for two deployment targets, edge and cloud, achieving higher accuracy than frontier models at up to 49x lower cost.
articles.title: Exowatt beats frontier models on accuracy with SageMaker serverless model customization

articles.author: Kiowa Jackson
articles.description: Fleet-wide computer vision needs a model per camera, not one model for the whole fleet. This post presents a working Amazon SageMaker SDK v3 reference architecture that trains, quality-gates, compiles per-camera models with SageMaker Neo, and versions thousands of them, with an AWS Step Functions layer pacing fleet-scale retraining within account quotas.
articles.title: Fleet-wide computer vision lifecycle at the edge with SageMaker SDK v3

articles.author: Claudio Mazzoni
articles.description: Every time an agent takes a step, it re-reads its entire context before acting. Here is how prompt caching for OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock lets your agent remember, cutting input cost and latency without resending the same tools, instructions, and history every turn.
articles.title: Groundhog Day for AI agents: Prompt caching patterns for using OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock

articles.author: Prabhakar Chandrasekaran
articles.description: Build enterprise agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with the AWS CDK: an agent that routes across two knowledge bases, retrieves through the AgentCore Gateway, and returns grounded, cited answers, with seven layers of observability and both on-demand and continuous evaluation, all deployed as a single CDK application.
articles.title: Build agentic retrieval on a Managed Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base with CDK

articles.author: Daniel Quang
articles.description: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI trains models on the outcome of a whole multi-step task rather than labeled steps. This hands-on guide walks the full pipeline using Wordle: deploying the agent and reward on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preparing the dataset, training, and evaluating at serving settings.
articles.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide

articles.author: Lauren Eterno
articles.description: Updating a SageMaker AI endpoint that has Application Auto Scaling registered makes AWS CloudFormation and AWS CDK deployments fail. This post shows how to build a reusable AWS CDK construct with CloudFormation custom resources that deregisters and re-registers auto scaling automatically, so you can update the endpoint and its scaling in a single deployment.
articles.title: Orchestrating SageMaker AI endpoint auto scaling with AWS CDK

articles.author: Amit Makashir
articles.description: Amazon Quick Sight layer maps now support Point and LineString geometry from the same GeoJSON workflow, so you can plot store locations and the routes between them. This post covers the dataset and GeoJSON structure layer maps require, when to choose points or lines, and techniques for viewport control, layering geometries, and dynamic GeoJSON updates.
articles.title: Visualize points and routes with GeoJSON in Amazon Quick Sight layer maps

articles.author: Subbu Dandamudi
articles.description: Bayer Crop Science built the Agentic Decision Engine (ADE), a multi-agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that lets breeders, analysts, and researchers ask natural language questions about their analytics platform. This post covers the ADE architecture, five design decisions, and how the team prepared it for production with AWS Unified Operations.
articles.title: How Bayer Crop Science built an agentic decision engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with AWS Unified Operations
